seed: Undo has to hand back the PICKING as well as the drawing. Sweep a band round two boxes, stack them, and press Undo: the boxes come back, the band comes back, and the two boxes must be picked again, or the next thing you do is sweep the same band a second time. Same for a delete: the boxes come back picked, so pressing Backspace again removes the same two. Every claim here is an expectPicked step, because a snapshot cannot photograph a pick that has gone missing - the rows just sit there unhighlighted and the walk passes.

steps.note: a rubber band drawn round both boxes: both picked, the band still on screen
the two boxes are one stack now, the band has come down, and the stack itself is what is picked
THE TEST: one Undo takes the stack apart, puts the band back AND picks the two boxes again, so Stack Selection is there to press a second time without sweeping anything (2026-09-08)
forward again in one press, and the stack it puts back is picked the way it was
Backspace over a band that caught layers removes the ones it caught: both boxes gone, nothing picked
THE OTHER TEST: the two boxes come back PICKED, which is the only way the next Backspace can mean anything
and pressing Backspace straight after the undo really does remove the same two again, which is the sentence the bug report was written in
